deployRoot.description: UNC (\\server\share), rooted local (C:\path), or volume-relative (\Share) for media whose drive letter cannot be known at build time. Never contains '..'. OPTIONAL: an image built without one reaches the Welcome screen with an empty share box and a hint telling the technician to supply it, rather than failing to boot.

credential.description: A username and nothing else. The secret lives in Control\share-credential.json, written by Set-HDTShareCredential (DESIGN 6.3).

folders.description: The folders the console draws, one list per category. A folder a document names is drawn whether or not it is listed here; a folder with nothing in it exists only here, which is what lets one be made before anything is put in it. Nothing the engine reads.

background.description: The image WinPE shows behind everything, copied into the image as \Windows\System32\winpe.jpg. It must be a JPEG: WinPE reads that one file under that one name, so any other format is carried into the image and never shown. MDT's custom background bitmap file. A path relative to the share, or a rooted one on the build host.

unattend.description: A WinPE answer file, copied into the image as \Unattend.xml and handed to wpeinit as -unattend:. This is what sets the WinPE firewall, the display, the page file and any RunSynchronous command - the settings wpeinit accepts, and the supported way to build an image with them rather than typing wpeutil at a prompt. It is NOT the deployed OS's unattend.xml; that belongs to the sequence. A path relative to the share, or a rooted one on the build host - exactly like extraContent's source, and for the same reason: the file an administrator browses to is wherever they keep it.

timeZone.description: The time zone WinPE runs in, as a Windows time zone id - 'Israel Standard Time', not '+02:00'. WinPE has no time zone setting in its answer file (wpeinit accepts eight Microsoft-Windows-Setup settings and TimeZone is not one of them), so an image runs on whatever its registry carries - Pacific Standard Time out of the ADK. Named here, Update-HDTBootImage runs dism /Image:<mount> /Set-TimeZone against the mounted WIM at build time, so a change needs a rebuild. Run Get-HDTTimeZone for the ids; tzutil is not in WinPE and is not what applies this.

promptForKey.description: Whether the ISO stops at 'Press any key to boot from CD or DVD'. False - the default, and what every image built before this key existed did - selects efisys_noprompt.bin, so a machine nobody is standing at boots without a keypress. True asks for the prompt back, which is what somebody wants when a machine's boot order still has the DVD first and it has to be able to fall through to the disk. UEFI only: the BIOS boot sector has no quiet variant.

rootCertificates.description: Certificate authority certificates imported into WinPE's Local Machine Root store at boot. WinPE starts with Microsoft's roots and nothing else, so an internal CA is trusted by every domain-joined machine and by no machine that has just booted a WIM. Public certificates only - a .pfx here would put a private key in the trusted root store. Each is a path relative to the share, or a rooted one on the build host.

clientCertificate.description: A .pfx imported into WinPE's Local Machine My store at boot, for a network that authenticates the machine before it gives it an address - 802.1X on the switch port, or PKI client authentication. Its password is NOT in this document: Set-HDTBootImageCertificatePassword writes it to Control\certificate-password.json. A path relative to the share, or a rooted one on the build host.

entryCommand.description: What startnet.cmd launches. Empty means the builder's default deployment payload.

startCommand.description: Commands startnet.cmd runs in order AFTER wpeinit and BEFORE the entry command. This is what makes extraContent useful: copying BGInfo or a VNC server into the image starts nothing, and the entry command is the deployment, which does not return. After wpeinit, so a tool that needs the network has one.

skip.description: MDT's Skip* properties for the Welcome screen. These four live in the boot image, not in rules.yaml, because the Welcome screen runs before the share is reachable. An omitted rule means the workspace said nothing, which is NOT the same as false: Get-HDTWizardSkip's defaults are what keep an unattended image unattended.

staticIp.description: Hide the static IP pane; DHCP is used.

deployRoot.description: Hide the share box; bootstrap.json's value is used.

credential.description: Hide the account pane; the embedded credential is used.

items.description: Levels separated by a single backslash, with nothing before the first or after the last.

destination.description: A path inside the image, rooted at the image and free of '..'.
